newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar up vs mark, boosted by mark sales vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar up vs mark, boosted by mark sales vs yen.

text.p: 0635 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar edged higher against the mark, briefly hitting a fresh 41-month high in late Tokyo trade on Thursday after the German currency lost ground against the yen on sales from Japanese exporters and trust banks.
Speculative short-covering in the dollar against the mark triggered stop-loss buy orders at 1.7620 marks, boosting the greenback as high as 1.7664 marks, dealers said.
"The dollar/mark rate rose mainly due to the mark's fall against the yen. Sales by Japanese trust banks stood out in particular," a Japanese commercial bank dealer said.

The German currency was also vulnerable to speculative sales against the dollar and the pound ahead of an announcement on interest rates later today by the Bank of England (BOE) Monetary Policy Committee.

The market has been factoring in a credit tightening by the BOE, keeping the mark's undertone extremely bearish against the pound, dealers said. Many operators expect a 25 basis point rise, but they had mixed views on the impact on the market.
"The pound has been overbought against the mark recently. The actual news of a 25 basis point rate rise could trigger profit-taking in the pound," a city bank dealer said.
Meanwhile, the commercial bank dealer said that news of a credit tightening could clear the way for the pound to climb above the crucial 3.0-mark level in the near future.
At 0714 GMT, sterling was firmer at 2.9730/40 marks, compared with 2.9640/50 marks in early Tokyo trade.
The mark stood at 63.84/87 yen after falling as low as about 63.74 yen in Tokyo, its lowest level in nearly two years. The mark was at 64.15 yen in early Tokyo trade.
Dealers said a wave of sales by Japanese trust banks from around 64.20 yen capped the mark's upside.
Trust banks were also active sellers in dollar/yen, capping the greenback throughout the day.

"Trust bank offers were lined up from 113.00 to 112.65 yen, weighing heavily on the dollar," the city bank dealer said. "But bids by U.S. and European securities houses firmly protected the dollar around 112.50/60 yen."
Japanese importers were also detected buying dollars. Talk that public fund bodies and Japanese institutional investors were placing massive bids limited active sales, dealers said.
With Japan's current account data and a Japan-U.S. business council out of the way, the dollar/yen rate drifted aimlessly, led by moves in the crosses or dollar/mark, dealers said.

Dealers said dollar bids emerged briefly after the Jiji news service reported that the Ministry of Finance's Eisuke Sakakibara said Japan will not use exchange rates as an instrument of trade policy, but most participants ignored it.
The dollar closed at 112.71/81 yen and 1.7598/7608 marks in New York on Wednesday.
